title: The limbus test for the quantitative examination of eye mobility
summary: The study aims to determine normal values ​​of eye movement in the main directions of movement of the four rectus and two oblique eye muscles, measured in millimeters. For this purpose, the distance of eye movement is measured with a small ruler (the "Kestenbaum limbus test"). Subjects aged 2 to 100 years or older are examined.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
(none)
Exclusion criteria:
- Age < 2 years
- Paralysis of the extraocular muscles
- History of extraocular muscle surgery
- Myasthenia gravis
- Parkinson's disease
- Multiple sclerosis
- Endocrine orbitopathy
- Orbital inflammation
- Acute and subacute (eye) trauma
- Orbital fractures
- All CCDDs (congenital cranial dysinnervation disorders)
